description:
As the United States celebrates its 250th birthday, millions are watching spectacular fireworks, military flyovers, and historic tall ships. But behind the celebration lies a far more remarkable story.

How did thirteen British colonies become one of the world's most influential nations? Why were 56 men willing to risk everything by signing a single document? And why do the ideas written in the Declaration of Independence continue to shape political debate nearly two and a half centuries later?

In this episode, we retrace America's founding—from the Stamp Act and the Boston Tea Party to Thomas Paine's Common Sense, the drafting of the Declaration of Independence, and the extraordinary sacrifices made by the nation's founders. We also explore the four defining crises that reshaped the United States and examine why the principles of liberty, constitutional government, and individual rights continue to resonate around the world.
